title: Credit allowance with heavy-user limits
decision_task: Whether to sell variable-cost work (AI generation, research, messages, jobs) as unlimited, pure pay-as-you-go, or a plan allowance in credits with top-ups, and how to rate each action so heavy users don't erase margin.
applies_when: Delivery cost per customer varies widely with use (AI calls, data lookups, sends, minutes)
Customers want a predictable bill but usage differs a lot between them
The business offers several actions with very different cost or value
exclusions: Cost per customer is flat and low (credits add confusion for no margin benefit)
Buyers can't relate credits to anything they value and no estimator can be shown
No metering exists to count usage per customer
required_inputs: Usage metering per customer and action
Billing that supports allowances and top-ups
evidence_requirements: Per-customer variable cost for at least one full billing cycle
Share of total variable cost from the top 10% of customers
Cost per action type, versioned by date
Customer comprehension check of the credit unit (can they predict their bill?)
missing_data_behavior: No per-customer cost data: recommend metering first; no allowance numbers.
Cost distribution unknown: present the decision as a hypothesis and ask for the top-10% cost share.
alternatives_when_constrained: No metering: use a fair-use cap on the top plan and review manually monthly
Low volume: one plan plus a single paid add-on for the costly action
Small budget/no billing integration: sell prepaid packs by invoice
Missing cost data: use provider invoices ÷ active customers as an average and flag distribution as unknown

decision_branches.if: Cost per customer is flat and low
decision_branches.then: Keep a simple plan; credits add confusion.

decision_branches.if: Top-decile customers drive a large share of cost
decision_branches.then: Allowance with top-ups; check margin at full use.
Plan tiers with a fair-use cap instead of raw credits; test comprehension.

implementation_steps: Compute cost per customer per month; rank customers; record the top-decile cost share
List actions; set credit rates by value to the buyer, with a floor of cost / (1 − target margin)
Size each plan's allowance so a customer who uses it all still meets the margin floor
Offer clearly priced top-ups or a fair-use limit for the heavy tail rather than raising everyone's price
Show the credit cost before any expensive action and a balance meter; never auto-charge overage without consent
Re-rate actions when provider costs or value change, with notice

cash_and_labor_requirements.cash: Billing tool changes; none required to analyse
cash_and_labor_requirements.labor: Owner 2-4 h to review cost data

metrics: Contribution margin per customer (distribution, not just average)
Share of customers hitting allowance; top-up attach rate
Breakage (unused credits) tracked separately from earned margin
guardrails: Fully used allowance meets the margin floor; breakage is never the plan that makes the margin
No hidden overage; balance and per-action cost visible
Re-rating applies only with advance notice; purchased credits keep their stated value
Do not degrade the core promised outcome to save cost
observation_window: Two full billing cycles after launch or re-rating; heavy-user share reviewed monthly.
stop_conditions: Top-decile customers are contribution-negative after two cycles: re-rate or cap
Surprise-bill tickets or refunds rise: simplify the unit or add an estimator
Conversion drops versus the prior flat plan with no margin gain: revert
review_triggers: Owner corrects an input this playbook relies on
A metric or guardrail crosses its bound
The underlying source or platform rule changes
climbos_location: Plan engine (offer/economics diagnosis), PB-pricing-test variant, margin calculator, pricing page advice. Separately: ClimbOS's own credit pricing review (see GU.md arithmetic).

interpretation: Interpretation: Kyle's case for credits is mainly about cost concentration and the vendor's freedom to re-rate actions; buyer predictability is the cost. For small businesses the same logic applies to any capped package of variable work (e.g., included revisions, call minutes).
proposed_climbos_rule: Proposed ClimbOS rule: when a customer's variable cost per account varies by more than a set ratio, the engine checks the top-decile cost share and the margin of a fully used allowance before recommending flat or unlimited pricing; recommendations must pass the margin floor at full allowance use, excluding breakage.
disagreements: Book 12 warns usage pricing needs clear metering and understanding; GU-01 claims credits feel simple to buyers. Decide by a comprehension test: if owners cannot predict their monthly credit use within a reasonable band, prefer plan tiers with a fair-use cap. GU-03 predicts 10–100x cost falls; GU-01 says newest-model costs had not fallen by late 2025. Rule: price on current observed cost, never on forecast declines.

hypothetical_evaluation_cases.label: hypothetical

inputs_hypothetical.business: Booking app for salons with AI reply drafting

expected_behavior: Notes 70% average margin hides ten customers at about -$50 contribution each
Proposes an allowance whose full use costs at most $28 plus priced top-ups or a fair-use cap for the heavy tail
Asks for comprehension testing and a balance display
Labels the 70–80%/10% concentration figure as the author's experience, not a benchmark
hard_failure: Raising price for all customers as the only fix
Recommending unlimited usage on the strength of expected falling AI costs

notes: Proposed reference contract. Not executable; does not authorize publishing, sending or spending. Numbers in source references are dated author figures, never forecasts.
